Manage and refer urgently:
If shock/systolic BP < 80, give sodium chloride 0.9% 500mL IV over 30 minutes, repeat until systolic BP > 80. Continue 1L 6 hourly. Stop if breathing worsens.
ABNORMAL VAGINAL BLEEDING

Approach to the patient with abnormal vaginal bleeding not needing urgent attention: • Check for pregnancy 174. • Do a pelvic examination to check for pelvic masses, a speculum examination to visualise cervix and a cervical screen if needed 70. • If > 40 years, ask about menopausal symptoms: hot flushes, night sweats, vaginal dryness, mood changes, difficulty sleeping and sexual problems 74. If new bleeding occurs > 1 year after final period, refer within 2 weeks. • If patient is not menopausal, determine the type of bleeding problem:
Heavy or prolonged periods

• If bleeding from elsewhere like easy bruising/purple rash/bleeding gums, arrange FBC and refer to doctor next day. • If Hb < 12, treat for likely anaemia 44. • Give COC2 ethinylestradiol/ levonorgestrel 30mcg/150mcg for 3-6 months 170. If pregnancy desired or COC contraindicated3, discuss/refer. • Give ibuprofen4 400mg 8 hourly with/after food for 3 days. • If on injectable contraceptive or subdermal implant, reassure that abnormal bleeding is common in first 3 months.
- If abnormal bleeding persists > 3 months,

manage as breakthrough bleeding (see adjacent). • Refer the patient: - Same week if mass in abdomen - If no better after 3 months on treatment - If excessive bleeding after IUD insertion - If sexual abuse suspected - If history of foreign body inserted into
vagina.

• If weight change, pulse ≥ 100, tremor, weakness/ tiredness, dry skin, constipation or intolerance to cold or heat, check TSH. If abnormal, refer to doctor. • Give COC2 ethinylestradiol/ levonorgestrel 30mcg/150mcg for 3-6 months 170. If pregnancy desired or COC contraindicated3, discuss/refer.
Irregular periods (cycle < 21 days or
> 35 days)
Spotting between periods
• Assess for STI 62. • Check Hb: if Hb < 12, treat for likely anaemia 44. • Manage according to hormonal contraceptive method:

Oral contraceptive • Ensure correct use and reassure that spotting is common in first 3 months. • If > 24 hours diarrhoea/vomiting, advise to use condoms (continue for 7 days once diarrhoea/ vomiting resolved). • If on ART, rifampicin, phenytoin or carbamazepine, change to copper IUD or injectable 170. • If bleeding persists > 3 months: - If on progestogen-only pill and bleeding
troublesome, change method 170. - If on COC2, switch to COC containing lowest
dose of ethinylestradiol (ethinylestradiol/ levonorgestrel 30mcg/150mcg). If no better after 3 cycles, discuss.

Refer patient within 2 weeks if: • Patient complains of pelvic pain. • Bleeding persists > 1 week after STI treatment or after diarrhoea/vomiting stop. • Bleeding persists despite treatment. If pain during periods 72.
Injectable contraceptive or

subdermal implant • Reassure that spotting is common in first 3 months. • If bleeding troublesome, also give COC2 ethinylestradiol/ levonorgestrel 30mcg/150mcg. Duration depends on contraceptive method:
- If subdermal implant, give for
20 days. - If on injectable, give for 14 days. • If COC contraindicated3, give instead ibuprofen4 400mg 8 hourly with/after food for 3 days.
IUD • Reassure that spotting is common in first 3 months, is not harmful and usually resolves. • Give ibuprofen4 400mg 8 hourly with/after food for 3 days.
Bleeding
after sex
• Assess for STI 62. • If sexual assault 32, if abuse 33.

1If SBP < 80, pulse ≥ 100, respiratory rate > 30, confusion/restlessness, weakness, shock likely. 2Combined oral contraceptive. 3Avoid COC if smoker ≥ 35 years, migraines and ≥ 35 years old or visual disturbances, up to 6 weeks postpartum, BP ≥ 140/90, hypertension, CVD risk > 10%, blood clots, previous stroke, ischaemic heart disease or diabetes complications (eye, nerve, kidney damage). 4Avoid if peptic ulcer, asthma, hypertension, heart failure or kidney disease.
